# 25 low-odor, low-allergen earplug starting recipes — metric

## Read first: limits and safety

**These are formulation starting points, not finished medical devices.** No home-made product can honestly be called “medical-grade,” “hypoallergenic,” “odor-free,” or given an NRR/SNR without raw-material certification, ISO 10993 biocompatibility testing, ISO 13485 manufacturing, validated cleaning/packaging, shelf-life data, and regulatory clearance. “Hypoallergenic” is not a guarantee; patch-test every batch.

- Use only **pharmaceutical/cosmetic/food-grade** materials: white paraffin wax, USP petrolatum, USP mineral oil, USP castor oil, fragrance-free lanolin, cosmetic-grade botanical waxes/butters. Avoid candle wax with dye/fragrance, wax melts, crayons, scented petroleum jelly, menthol/Vicks, essential oils, tea tree, garlic/onion, vinegar, alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, household silicone sealant, Blue-Tack, or craft putty not labeled skin-safe.
- Anhydrous waxes have no meaningful pH. “Skin-neutral” here means **no added acid/alkali/fragrance/dye**, low peroxide/anisidine value, and an aqueous extract target of **pH 5.0–6.0** if tested.
- **Do not insert deeply.** Use a broad outer flange, keep it outside the canal, use single-use plugs, and never use with eardrum perforation, ventilation tubes, recent ear surgery, active infection, dermatitis, diabetes, or immunosuppression. Not for children under 5; choking hazard. Remove and seek ENT care for pain, discharge, hearing loss, tinnitus, or a retained fragment.
- DIY wax is **not a reliable water seal**. Custom swim molds are preferred. “W” grades require professional fit and leak testing.
- Melt waxes in a clean double boiler at **70–85 °C**; never over an open flame. Use a **0.1 g** scale. Do not add water to wax formulations.

## Grading key

- **Class:** **N** = noise; **W** = water; **E** = external-canal emollient/cerumen-mimetic, not a protector.
- **Initial designation:** **IND-A** = first-line bench prototype; **IND-B** = conditional/backup, one odor/allergen/mechanical limitation; **IND-C** = reference/classical only, not for canal use.
- **T** = target probe tack relative to refined beeswax, **B = 1.00**. Values are formulation targets, not measured clinical claims.
- **Odor:** **O0** no added fragrance/low odor; **O1** faint; **O2** noticeable.
- **Skin:** **S1** low-risk anhydrous; **S2** patch-test mandatory due to botanical/lanolin content; **S3** not for ear skin/canal.

## Common method for R01–R13

Melt paraffin and hard waxes at the stated temperature; add petrolatum/oils at **60–65 °C**; stir **5 min**; cool to **50–55 °C**; mold into **10–15 mm** diameter pellets, **8–12 mm** thick, with a **3–5 mm** broad outer flange; cure **24 h** at **20–25 °C**; store airtight, cool, dark. **R01–R13 are beeswax-free and target T ≥ 1.00B.**

### R01–R13: beeswax-free, tack ≥ beeswax target

| # | Composition for 25 g batch | Process | Distinctive characteristic | Initial designation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R01** | Paraffin 12.5 g; white petrolatum 8.75 g; microcrystalline wax 3.75 g | Melt 75 °C; cast 52 °C | Balanced firmness, cohesion, and low residue; best general N/W prototype | **IND-A/NW; T 1.2B; O0; S1** |
| **R02** | Paraffin 13.75 g; petrolatum 7.5 g; castor oil 3.75 g | Melt 70 °C; add castor at 60 °C | High tack with soft concha fit; castor can migrate | **IND-A/NW; T 1.3B; O0; S1** |
| **R03** | Paraffin 12.5 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; mineral oil 3.75 g | Melt 70 °C; add oil at 60 °C | Softer, quiet insertion; less water-resistant; noise/sleep use | **IND-A/N; T 1.1B; O0; S1** |
| **R04** | Paraffin 10 g; petrolatum 10 g; lanolin 5 g | Melt 70 °C; add lanolin at 60 °C | Maximum tack and emollience; lanolin allergy and odor risk | **IND-B/NW; T 1.4B; O1; S2** |
| **R05** | Paraffin 12 g; petrolatum 8 g; candelilla wax 4 g; castor oil 1 g | Melt 80 °C; add castor at 60 °C | Vegan high-tack, firm plug; faint wax odor | **IND-B/NW; T 1.25B; O1; S2** |
| **R06** | Paraffin 15 g; petrolatum 8 g; carnauba wax 2 g | Melt 85 °C; cast 55 °C | Hardest, high water resistance, but brittle; mechanical risk | **IND-B/N; T 1.0B; O1; S1** |
| **R07** | Paraffin 11.25 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; soy wax 5 g | Melt 75 °C | Soft vegan plug; soy allergen/odor risk | **IND-B/NW; T 1.15B; O2; S2** |
| **R08** | Paraffin 12.5 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; rice bran wax 3.75 g | Melt 80 °C | Firm, low-odor vegan; good water resistance | **IND-B/NW; T 1.1B; O1; S2** |
| **R09** | Paraffin 12.5 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; sunflower wax 3.75 g | Melt 80 °C | Firm vegan; lower tack than R05 | **IND-B/NW; T 1.05B; O1; S2** |
| **R10** | Paraffin 11.25 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; shea butter 5 g | Melt 70 °C; add shea at 60 °C | Soft emollient; shea odor/allergen; noise only | **IND-B/N; T 1.2B; O2; S2** |
| **R11** | Paraffin 12.5 g; petrolatum 8.75 g; cocoa butter 3.75 g | Melt 70 °C; add cocoa at 60 °C | Chocolate odor; softens at body temperature; noise only | **IND-B/N; T 1.1B; O2; S2** |
| **R12** | Paraffin 13.75 g; petrolatum 7.5 g; coconut oil 3.75 g | Melt 65 °C | Very soft, low melt, may migrate; not for water | **IND-B/N; T 1.0B; O1; S2** |
| **R13** | Paraffin 11.25 g; petrolatum 7.5 g; microcrystalline wax 3.75 g; castor oil 2.5 g | Melt 75 °C; add castor at 60 °C | Highest balanced tack/cohesion; best DIY water-seal candidate | **IND-A/NW; T 1.35B; O0; S1** |

## R14–R25: classical, contemporary, commercial-reference, and cerumen-mimetic

R14–R16 are historical/classical; R17–R20 are commercial or clinical-reference approaches; R21–R22 are home-made references; R23–R25 are **cerumen-mimetic candidates** targeting hydrophobicity, cohesion, low odor, and pH-neutrality. They do **not** claim antimicrobial action and are **not** for obstructive earwax.

| # | Composition | Process | Distinctive characteristic | Initial designation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R14** | Cotton wool 5 g; olive oil 3 mL | Mix; no heat | Classical oiled cotton; cheap but fibers/mess; not water protection | **IND-C/N; O2; S3** |
| **R15** | Cotton wool 5 g; petrolatum 5 g | Work together | Classical occlusive cotton; messy; fiber-shedding risk | **IND-C/N; O0; S3** |
| **R16** | Beeswax 5 g; paraffin 5 g; cotton wool 5 g | Melt 70 °C; embed cotton | Historical moldable cotton-core plug; high tack; not hypoallergenic | **IND-C/N; O1; S3** |
| **R17** | 100% platinum-cure silicone earplug putty, 2 g per ear | Use as supplied | Commercial swim/noise putty; best simple water option if fit is good | **IND-A/W*; O0; S1** |
| **R18** | Platinum-cure silicone part A 10 g + part B 10 g; 30 Shore A | Mix 1:1 by weight; cure 24 h at 23 °C | Custom professional mold; best fit/attenuation; needs ear impression | **IND-A/NW; O0; S1** |
| **R19** | EVA 18 g; petrolatum 2 g | Heat 70 °C; mold | Reheatable custom mold; hardens; heat/impaction risk | **IND-B/NW; O0; S1** |
| **R20** | Polycaprolactone 20 g | Melt 60 °C; mold | Reusable low-temperature mold; hardens; heat/impaction risk | **IND-B/NW; O0; S1** |
| **R21** | Gelatin 5 g; glycerin 10 g; water 10 g | Heat 80 °C; cool | Home-made moldable gel; water-soluble, microbial risk; not water protection | **IND-C/N; O2; S3** |
| **R22** | Cornstarch 10 g; petrolatum 10 g; mineral oil 5 g | Mix at 50 °C | Dough-like; crumbly/particulate; not water protection | **IND-C/N; O2; S3** |
| **R23** | Petrolatum 10 g; mineral oil 10 g; lanolin 5 g | Warm 50 °C; mix | Cerumen-mimetic emollient; closest cerumen feel; lanolin allergy risk | **IND-B/E; O2; S2** |
| **R24** | Squalane 10 g; petrolatum 10 g; paraffin 5 g | Melt 60 °C | Cerumen-mimetic; low odor/oxidation; equal/over cerumen in stability; cost caveat | **IND-A/E; O0; S1** |
| **R25** | Petrolatum 12.5 g; microcrystalline wax 7.5 g; castor oil 5 g | Melt 75 °C | Cerumen-mimetic with high cohesion/water resistance; not for impaction | **IND-B/NW/E; O0; S1** |

## Selection summary

- **Best first bench prototypes:** R01, R13, R24.
- **Highest tack:** R04 > R13 > R02, but R04 is lanolin-limited.
- **Best water-seal candidates:** R13, R01, and commercial R17/R18. DIY wax still needs professional fit.
- **Best cerumen-mimetic:** R24; R23 is emollient but lanolin-allergenic; R25 is more cohesive but too plug-like for cerumen-substitution use.
- **Do not designate for canal use:** R14–R16 and R21–R22.

**To move toward a real medical device:** require USP/Ph.Eur. raw-material CoAs, extractables/leachables, ISO 10993-5/-10/-23, HRIPT sensitization testing, bioburden/packaging validation, shelf-life, fit/attenuation testing to ANSI S3.19 or EN 352, and water-leak testing. Do not claim NRR/SNR or “hypoallergenic” before that work.
